task.description: HARD GATE. Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req024-event-type-registry.md (commit 0b3057f) on branch feature/WF02-REQ024-20260816 against REQ-024's 5 acceptance criteria and WF-02 Step 1b's checklist. CODE-DESIGNER made a real library decision here (hand-rolled JSON Schema validator vs. ex_json_schema, decided against adding a new dependency) -- independently re-verify this decision's factual basis against R-Co source yourself, don't just accept the design doc's reasoning. Also verify no new docs/migration/decisions/ record was needed and that this determination is itself sound (i.e. check whether it really doesn't cross 0001/0002/0003's bar for requiring one).
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains an event_type_registry migration (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022) applying cleanly
register_type/2 rejects a second registration with the same (name, schema_version) with a distinct, testable error, not a generic changeset failure
validate_payload/2 against a payload missing a required field returns a failure result whose detail names the specific field_path (JSON Pointer form) and constraint, not just a boolean false
get_type/1 against an unregistered name returns an explicit :unknown_event_type-shaped error rather than nil or an exception
the moduledoc names the JSON Schema validation library choice as an explicit open question for CODE-DESIGNER, not a silently made decision

result.summary: AC1-4 (migration spec, register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2) are concretely specified with full @spec-style signatures, ordered behavior, and explicit {:ok,_}|{:error,_} shapes -- no TBD/deferral language found (grep clean). The JSON Schema library decision (design S1) was independently re-verified against R-Co source, not taken on the design's word: src/tools/json_schema.zig's own moduledoc (lines 21-25) states verbatim that $ref/allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/patternProperties/pattern/format/dependencies/tuple-form items are 'deliberately NOT implemented; unknown keywords remain silently ignored' -- and src/design/spc-01-sub-process-interface-contract.md's well-formedness table (lines 273-282) lists the exact same 8-keyword supported set the design quotes in its S1.1. The design's characterization is accurate, not exaggerated. mix.exs/mix.lock were read directly (deps block, lines 33-41): ecto_sql, postgrex, plug, bandit, jason, stream_data, ueberauth_oidcc -- no ex_json_schema or any JSON-Schema package present, confirming S1's factual premise. On the decision-record question: 0001/0002/0003's own openings were re-read independently -- 0001 is a framework-wide migration (Plug/Bandit -> Phoenix across 24 route modules), 0002 is a new mix.exs auth dependency with security-critical JIT-provisioning scope, 0003 is the schema-per-tenant strategy governing every future migration project-wide. REQ-024's choice not to add ex_json_schema adds zero mix.exs entries and has no dependency-graph/licensing/upgrade consequence -- a materially narrower bar than any of the three, and REQ-028 (merged, status: done) hand-rolled its own graph validator with no decision record either, corroborating the precedent claim. I concur: no new docs/migration/decisions/ record is needed here. The schema_version-monotonic rule (S4.1 callout) is correctly and explicitly flagged as a Letflow-specific rule beyond R-Co, not silently presented as existing R-Co behavior -- confirmed against registry.zig having no such check. HOWEVER: the design FAILS on tenant-prefix threading, independently checked against lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's actual code (not the design's description of it). Design S4's opening interface note asserts register_type/2, validate_payload/3, and get_type/2 must each take prefix :: String.t() directly from the caller, justified by the claim this is done 'the same way Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 does'. That citation is factually wrong: replay_migrations/2's actual signature (tenant_provisioning.ex lines 153-160) takes tenant_id, not prefix -- it internally resolves schema_name via Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id) (line 161) and returns {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} (line 163) if no Registration row exists, i.e. the module owns prefix derivation and the not-provisioned error case; the caller never supplies or knows a raw prefix string. Every other real public function in this module (schema_name_for_tenant/1, provision_tenant_schema/1) is likewise tenant_id-in, not prefix-in. This is not just a wrong citation: the design's S6 cross-module-dependencies list never names schema_name_for_tenant/1 or Registration as how a caller obtains the prefix value it's supposed to pass -- the actual mechanism is completely unspecified. REQ-025's Store.append/1 (the design's own named first consumer, S6) has no way to know from this document whether it should call schema_name_for_tenant/1 (pure, no provisioning check -- would silently query a schema that may not exist) or look up Registration itself (duplicating replay_migrations/2's internal logic) to get the prefix. The design's error unions for register_type/2 (S4.1), validate_payload/3 (S4.2), and get_type/2 (S4.3) also have no :tenant_not_provisioned-equivalent case, silently dropping the error path replay_migrations/2 has for exactly this situation. This fails Step 1b check (b) (signature not fully specified -- prefix's provenance and the not-provisioned case are unaddressed) and check (d) (the real cross-module dependency for deriving/validating prefix is not listed).

issues.description: Design S4's interface note requires register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2 to accept prefix :: String.t() directly from the caller, citing Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 as precedent for this convention. Verified directly against lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex: replay_migrations/2 (lines 153-181) actually takes tenant_id, not prefix, and internally resolves schema_name via a Registration lookup (Repo.get_by, line 161), returning {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} when no Registration row exists (line 163). No public function in tenant_provisioning.ex takes a raw prefix string from a caller. The design's S6 cross-module-dependencies section never names schema_name_for_tenant/1 or Registration as the mechanism a caller uses to obtain the prefix value it must pass, and none of S4.1/S4.2/S4.3's error unions carry a :tenant_not_provisioned-equivalent case. This leaves the actual, real question -- how does REQ-025's Store.append/1 (this design's own named first caller) obtain a correct prefix value, and what happens if the tenant isn't provisioned -- completely unspecified, which is exactly the kind of interface ambiguity Step 1b exists to catch before ELIXIR-DEV has to guess.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: revise req024-event-type-registry.md S4 so register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2 either (a) take tenant_id and internally resolve schema_name via Letflow.TenantProvisioning (naming that as a real S6 cross-module dependency), matching replay_migrations/2's actual convention including a :tenant_not_provisioned-equivalent error case, or (b) keep prefix :: String.t() but explicitly name the resolution mechanism the caller is expected to use and the error case for an unprovisioned tenant -- either is acceptable, but the current draft asserts a precedent that does not match the cited file and leaves the derivation path completely unstated.
